name: Orange Cream
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: eggs (omitting the whites of two)
ingredients.originalText: six eggs (omitting the whites of two)

instructions.text: Beat very light six eggs, omitting the whites of two
Have ready a pint of orange juice and stir it gradually into the beaten egg, alternately with a pound of powdered loaf-sugar
Put into a porcelain skillet the yellow rind of one orange, pared very thin
Pour the mixture upon it and set it over a slow fire
Simmer it steadily, stirring it all the time
When nearly ready to boil, take it off and remove the orange-peel
Put the mixture into glasses to get cold

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Beat very light six eggs, omitting the whites of two
2. Have ready a pint of orange juice and stir it gradually into the beaten egg, alternately with a pound of powdered loaf-sugar
3. Put into a porcelain skillet the yellow rind of one orange, pared very thin
4. Pour the mixture upon it and set it over a slow fire
5. Simmer it steadily, stirring it all the time
6. When nearly ready to boil, take it off and remove the orange-peel
7. Put the mixture into glasses to get cold
